I'm going to be honest about something most women on Wegovy® and Ozempic® don't want to admit out loud.

The only thing that fixed my constipation wasn't anything my prescriber recommended. It wasn't anything the pharmacist suggested. It wasn't anything I found in the supplement aisle. It wasn't the $40 "gentle" laxative tea my well-meaning sister mailed me. It wasn't the prescription Senna squares my GP wrote up after my third complaint.

I tried all of it. None of it worked.

If you're on Wegovy®, Ozempic®, Mounjaro®, Zepbound®, or Foundayo™ and you've spent the last three months building a graveyard of laxatives in your bathroom cabinet — read this. The reason none of it has worked has nothing to do with you. It has to do with what your medication is actually doing inside your body.

I started Wegovy® eleven months ago. By month three I was down 22 pounds. By month seven, 41. I should have been thrilled. Instead I was sitting on my bathroom floor at 6 AM crying because I hadn't gone in eight days.

Here's what I tried. In order. Because I want you to recognize yourself somewhere on this list.

Miralax. $15. Drank it for two weeks. The first three days I went a little. Then it stopped — but the bloating was worse. My pants didn't fit by Friday afternoon. My stomach looked seven months pregnant.

Fiber gummies. $20. Took them for a month. Stomach got harder, not softer. I'd lie down at night and you could see the outline of where the food was sitting in my abdomen. It sat in my gut like a rock.

That "gentle" laxative tea. $40. A box. Forty dollars for a small box of tea bags that did nothing. I threw the rest of the box in the trash.

Dulcolax. $13. Got the cramps. Got the 4 AM agony. Did not get the relief.

Prescription senna squares. Miserable. Embarrassing to ask my doctor for. Cramps so bad I missed work twice. And I still couldn't go.

Magnesium oxide from the supplement aisle. $12. Did absolutely nothing. (I learned later why — your body absorbs about 4% of magnesium oxide. The label said 500mg. I was getting maybe 20mg of usable magnesium per dose.)

Probiotic. $40. Marketed for "digestive support." Six weeks. No change.

A "GLP-1 daily" multivitamin from Amazon. $42. Came in two days. Took it for two months. If anything, the bloating got worse.

I added it up one morning. Over $180 in three months on supplements and laxatives that did nothing or made me feel worse. I had a discontinuation appointment scheduled with my prescriber for that Wednesday. I was going to throw away my 41 pounds because I couldn't take another night of this.

Then my niece — who's a pharmacy tech in Phoenix — sent me a 12-minute video that explained why every single thing on that list was the wrong mechanism for what's actually happening on a GLP-1.

It changed everything.

Here's what no one had explained to me before:

Your GLP-1 medication works by slowing your gastric emptying by 50% or more. That's the therapeutic mechanism. That's why you stop being hungry. That's why I lost 41 pounds.

But the same slowed motility doesn't stop at your stomach. It runs your entire digestive system. Stool sits longer. Dries out. Compacts. Food in the stomach for twice as long as it should be ferments — that's where the sulfur burps come from, by the way. Bacteria breaking down food in a stomach that should have already emptied.

This is why every single product on my list failed for the same reason:

Fiber doesn't work on a GLP-1 because fiber adds bulk that needs gut motility to push it through. My motility was being intentionally suppressed by my Wegovy®. I was adding bulk to a system that couldn't move bulk. It just makes a bigger backup.

Stimulant laxatives don't work because they trigger contractions that my Wegovy® was designed to suppress. The two drugs fought each other inside my body. I felt the cramping. I didn't get the relief. The GLP-1 wins every single time. Dulcolax, Senna, that "gentle" tea — same mechanism, same failure.

Magnesium oxide doesn't work because oxide is the cheapest, least bioavailable form. 4% of it gets absorbed. The label was lying to me with technical truth.

Probiotics didn't work because the problem wasn't my microbiome. The problem was upstream of it.

I needed something designed for Ozempic® constipation. Not a normal one.

The video walked through what actually works:

Magnesium glycinate — pulls water into the gut osmotically. It doesn't require contractions. It works WITH a slowed system instead of fighting it. Bioavailable form your body actually absorbs.

Ginger root extract standardized to 5% gingerols — a natural prokinetic. Helps your stomach empty so food doesn't sit and rot. Stops the fermentation that causes the sulfur burps. Doesn't force contractions, so it doesn't fight your medication.

Methylcobalamin B12 — the active form, not the cheap synthetic. Addresses the energy depletion that comes from reduced calorie intake and impaired absorption.

Three nutrients. Right forms. Designed for the slowed-on-purpose mechanism your medication creates.

The video pointed me to a small brand called GLP-1 SOS™. Magnesium glycinate verified at the labeled dose. Ginger root standardized to 5.1% gingerols by HPLC. Methylcobalamin B12 in the active form. Manufactured in an FDA-registered facility in Utah. Third-party Certificate of Analysis on every batch.

It costs $24.99 for a 30-day supply.

I was twelve hours from canceling a $1,400-a-month medication. Twenty-five dollars to try one more thing wasn't a risk. It was less than half of what I'd spent on the laxative tea alone.

I cancelled the discontinuation appointment that morning. I ordered GLP-1 SOS™ that afternoon.

Day 1: nothing.

Day 2: nothing.

Day 3: nothing. I started to think it was another lie.

Day 4: I went. Gently. No cramping. No urgency. Just relief.

48 hours after my first dose, the sulfur burps stopped completely. By week two I was sleeping through the night without 4 AM cramps. By week three I had energy at 3 PM for the first time since I'd started Wegovy®. By week four my husband Tom and I went out to dinner and I sat for two hours and I never once excused myself.

I'm still on Wegovy®. Still down to 158. A1C 5.3 — best it's been in twenty years.

It's been four months now. I'm going like clockwork. No cramping. No bloating. No sulfur burps. No bathroom emergencies. No more mornings on the floor.

If you're sitting in your bathroom right now reading this with a graveyard of failed laxatives on your counter — please hear me. Save your money. Stop buying the next $20, $40, $90 product that's the same wrong mechanism as the previous eight.

You don't need a different brand. You don't need a different dose. You need a different mechanism — one designed for Ozempic® constipation, not a normal one.

That's GLP-1 SOS™. 27,000+ people on Ozempic®, Wegovy®, Mounjaro®, Zepbound®, and Foundayo™ are on it now. Made in the USA. FDA-registered facility. Third-party tested. 60-day money-back guarantee. $24.99 for a 30-day supply.

Tap below.
https://glp1sos.com

EDIT: A few people messaged that they bought "GLP-1 SOS" on Amazon and felt nothing. There are knockoffs sold under similar names. The real GLP-1 SOS™ ships ONLY from glp1sos.com. They don't sell on Amazon. Most Amazon supplements sit in heat-damaged warehouses that destroy magnesium and ginger anyway. Buy direct.

P.S. Save your money. The next $20, $40, $90 product is going to be the same wrong mechanism as the eight that came before it. Stop the receipt. The supplement that actually addresses the slowed-on-purpose mechanism is $24.99 — less than half of what you spent on the "gentle" tea that did nothing.

P.P.S. If you're already booked for a discontinuation appointment — please don't click submit before you try this one thing. The 41 pounds I almost threw away cost me eleven months of work. Twenty-five dollars and four days saved them. Finally feel normal on your GLP-1. https://glp1sos.com
